p1793.title: fix(1789): specialize termination analysis without combinatorial products
p1793.body:
Refs #1789. A follow-up to #1791: the effective diff against `main` is 6 files.

## Problem
Since #1791, the input-specific termination certificate runs on the production corpus. But it substituted every immutable join binding into each rule, and production schemas multiply out: it exhausted its 2^18-statement bound before deciding. In order, it named:
- `dl:disjointUnion-disjoint`: 45,796 ground pairs from 262,144+ matches;
- `dl:property-chain`: 88,382 specializations, because list member cells were unlinked to their list.

## Changes (`crates/logic/src/physical/seminaive/joint/input/admission.rs`, `property.rs`, `chase.rs`)
- **Discharge and project.** A fully bound immutable atom is a ground source row that no termination rung reads, so it is dropped. Join bindings that agree on every still-read variable specialize once.
- **Ground laws are witnessed once.** When every still-read variable is bound by immutable rows, each specialization is ground: none can carry a null, and all fire on the same predicates. One specialization represents the rule, and the join stops at its first match.
- **Member cells read their own list.** `analysis_body` left list-member cells unconstrained, so a list operator paired every cell of every list. Property layouts now record each member cell's list head (`analysis_list_cells`, carried on `StatementRule::list_cells`).
  - When `rdf:first`/`rdf:rest` are proved immutable, the join binds each cell to the cells reachable from that head through `rdf:rest\*`, shared tails included, before reading it.
  - Past the analysis bound, cells stay unconstrained: coarser, but every firing is still covered.
  - Value flow is unchanged.
- **Honest exhaustion.** The refusal names the exhausting rule with its immutable-match and distinct-specialization counts. If the finer enriched pass cannot complete, the decided first-pass certificate stands, rather than falling back to the source-independent template.

## Tests (admission level; no chase execution)
- `a_pairwise_list_law_past_the_analysis_bound_is_witnessed_once`: a 600-member disjoint union (360,000 pairs) beside a minimum restriction certifies.
- `a_list_operator_reads_only_the_cells_of_its_own_list`: a property chain among 600 unrelated two-member lists (1.44M unlinked cell pairs) certifies.
- Each test fails with exactly its own mechanism disabled.

An end-to-end version was dropped. A 600-member disjoint union really entails 360,000 `disjointWith` facts, and materializing them OOMs the build slice. #1792 tracks the quadratic class analysis that dominates that run.

## Verification
- `cargo nextest run -p gmeow-logic`: 2217 run, 167 failed. The failure set is **identical** to `main`'s; all 167 need producer fixtures.
- Clippy reports no hits on changed lines.
- Production run in progress. I'll comment with the stage-reason result. Full `make check` cannot pass until production reasoning is admitted; that is the remaining #1789 work, and it is not a regression from this PR.

p1798.title: feat(1796): run the restricted chase Datalog-first
p1798.body:
Part 1 of #1796, the precondition for the restricted-chase termination certificate.

## Problem
The joint materializer gathered every producer against one frozen round snapshot (*"Every producer reads the same cross-world frozen round"*). So an existential trigger was checked **before** the Datalog consequences of earlier witnesses existed. For example, with `JournalEntry ⊑ ≥2 journalEntryPostings.Posting`, an inverse property, and `Posting ⊑ ∃postingJournalEntry.JournalEntry`:
- the posting's back edge to its entry was derived in the same round in which the reverse restriction was checked;
- so a fresh entry was minted every round, and the chase never terminated, even though the authored axioms are satisfiable with one witness.

## Change (`crates/logic/src/physical/seminaive/joint.rs`)
- **Datalog-first rounds.** Within each stratum, witness-minting producers (existential rules and generative witness families, gmeow's only witness mint sites) fire only in a round that follows a Datalog-only round with nothing left to add.
- **No lost triggers.** Witness producers read every row committed since they last gathered: a per-world generative row span plus accumulated changed predicates. Semi-naive evaluation therefore loses no trigger across the Datalog-only rounds they sit out.
- **Completion order.** A stratum concludes blocked or complete only after its witness producers have had their round.
- **Same guarantees.** It stays deterministic (sorted commit unchanged) and mints a subset of the interleaved schedule's witnesses.
- **Doctrine.** `slices/grounding/logic/design/LOGIC-PERFORMANCE.md` records the rule in its chase doctrine.

## Tests
- `an_inverse_back_edge_satisfies_the_reverse_restriction_under_datalog_first`: the inverse-pair program closes with **one** witness and the derived back edge. With Datalog-first disabled it **exhausts** its budget, verified by mutation.
- Two regressions caught by existing tests during development are fixed:
  - Blocked strata must still give witness producers their round (`empty_nominal_guard_remains_in_joint_invention_admission`).
  - The generative round must re-evaluate the Datalog producers' last span, so value-interpretation withholding is not lost (`functional_property_distinct_xml_literals_are_withheld`, `unknown_value_interpretations_withhold_only_the_affected_law`).

## Verification
- `cargo nextest run -p gmeow-logic`: 2215 run, 167 failed. The failure set is **identical** to `main`'s; all 167 need producer fixtures.
- `cargo nextest run -p gmeow-pipeline -E 'test(/stages::reason|witness|chase/)'`: 16/23 pass. The 7 failures all need `GMEOW_TEST_FIXTURE_MANIFEST` or the bundle-import cache.
- Clippy reports no hits on changed lines.

## Next
Part 2 adds the **restricted joint acyclicity** rung (sound under this schedule) so such programs are *certified* and run without a budget. Generated outputs may change when the producer next runs, because fewer witnesses are minted.

p1799.title: feat(1796): certify restricted joint acyclicity
p1799.body:
Part 2 of #1796, stacked on #1798 (Datalog-first schedule).

Adds the **restricted joint acyclicity** (RJA) rung to the termination certificate ladder (Carral, Dragoste & Krötzsch 2017, Def. 4). An edge v→w of the JA dependency graph is dropped when the Datalog closure of the frozen consumer body, the producer head and the producer body already satisfies the consumer head. Genuine inverse-pair existential cycles (`p ⊑ ∃r`, `r⁻` back-edge) therefore certify and run **without a budget**.

- Sound only for the Datalog-first restricted chase (#1798).
- Runs as the **last** rung, so programs already certified by WA/JA/SWA/MSA keep their class. Rank: RJA=5.
- Poset meets: RJA∧SWA=WA, RJA∧MSA=JA.
- Only exact Datalog rules feed the blocking closure. Any rule with a numeric guard, `distinct`, negation or witness minting is excluded, so guarded rules never block a trigger.
- The LOGIC-PERFORMANCE.md ladder doctrine names the rung.

Tests: `chase.tests.rs` (certifies the inverse pair; refuses without the inverse; meets with incomparable classes; a guarded rule doesn't block) and `list_tests.rs` (the inverse pair runs unbudgeted with one witness).

Mutation checks:
- Never blocking fails the certify and unbudgeted tests.
- Dropping the `distinct` exclusion fails the guard test.

The gmeow-logic regression matches the main baseline exactly: 2054 passed, 167 failed, and the failures are the same set as on main.

Upstream lift to purrdf is tracked in #1797.

p1800.title: fix(1795): sharpen termination-statement encoding and bind closed relations
p1800.body:
Fixes #1795. Stacked on #1793.

The input-specific termination certificate was refusing production because of encoding coarseness, not real cycles. Two commits:

**`7a285ccfb`: per-atom encoding, fresh-null keys, count-1 minimums**
- **P2:** the global `fixed_relations` switch is gone.
  - Constant-predicate atoms keep binary, class-refined positions. Only variable-predicate atoms go to the pair relations.
  - Weak acyclicity links the two encodings only along subject/object flows with matching class keys.
  - JA, SWA and MSA get non-existential Datalog bridge rules between the encodings.
- **P3:** a head position whose partner is a fresh existential gets the key `Null`, which feeds only wildcard reads. Stored nulls are never rewritten: sameAs only derives, refutations only write `instanceOf Nothing`, and DL blocking reuses an older witness.
- **P4:** a minimum family with count 1 is analysed with one witness and no `differentFrom`. The count stays in the deduplication key. Such a family still goes through WA only: letting it use the other rungs made an existing test use more than 24 GB.

**`4e7c7f2a7`: closed witness-free relations (P1)**
- A predicate, or a (predicate, constant object) pair, counts as closed when every producer that can write it creates no witnesses and reads only immutable or closed relations. Membership is decided by dropping candidates until stable.
- The closure is a semi-naive Datalog fixpoint over the source rows and feeds specialization. The induction proof is in the `Closure` doc comment.
- If the closure exceeds the 2^18 bound, the certificate falls back to immutable relations only, and the refusal names the reason.
- When the first pass certifies, the 1,383 s second pass is skipped.

**Tests and mutation checks:**
- 7 chase tests, 6 input tests and 4 admission tests.
- Disabling each mechanism fails at least one test.
- With the writer check disabled, all three refusal tests wrongly certify.
- These cases stay refused, as intended:
  - `p range R` with `R ⊑ ≥1 p`;
  - a subclass path back into the restriction;
  - the finance inverse pair, which is handled in #1796 (#1798 and #1799).

**Regression:**
- gmeow-logic: the 167 failures are the same set as the baseline.
- `stages::reason`: the same 3 failures as on unmodified code.
- Clippy reports nothing new on changed lines.

**Not yet verified:** the effect on the production refusal (11,202 violations), pending a combined production run.

p1801.title: perf(1757): compute joint acyclicity in linear Horn propagation
p1801.body:
Part of #1757. This targets `main` directly and is independent of the RJA stack.

**Problem:** joint acyclicity was cubic in program size.
- For every existential, `move_set` re-scanned every flow until nothing changed.
- Each `move_contains` call scanned the whole position universe twice.
- The edge loop rescanned all existentials for every edge and recomputed refined positions on every check.

Measured on a synthetic program: doubling the size made it 8.4× slower (1.6 s → 13.4 s). A 25k-rule statement program would take hours. The input-specific certifier reaches JA once #1796 lets witness families leave the weak-acyclicity-only path, which is how this surfaced.

**Fix:**
- A move set Ω_v is a Horn least fixpoint: a flow fires when *all* its body positions are covered. So each move set is now one **Dowling–Gallier counter propagation** (1984) over a `MoveIndex` built once, linear in program size.
- The conservative sibling rule (a slot with both wildcard and constant refinements) is precomputed per slot. The first time a slot is occupied, all of its body positions are covered at once.
- Consumer frontier positions and rule→existential owners are indexed once, in `JointGraph`.
- Acyclicity is a single **Kahn** elimination. `node_reaches_self` stays for SWA, which checks only a subset of nodes.

**Equivalence:** a 5,000-program differential run against the previous implementation, scratch only and not committed, matched every verdict and every evidence string, edge counts included. The programs were random and mixed wildcard and constant refinements, inverses and cycles: 3,486 certified and 1,514 refused.

**Speed:** with 200 existential rules and 2,000 Datalog rules, the check drops from 13.4 s to 6 ms. With 2,000 and 20,000 it takes 177 ms.

**Regression:** the gmeow-logic failure set matches main exactly (167, the same set). Clippy reports nothing new on changed lines.

p1804.title: fix(slices): repair the corpus inconsistencies native reasoning exposed
p1804.body:
Found while making native reasoning run on the production corpus (#1757, PR #1802). The production `rl-default` world was **genuinely inconsistent**: the native reasoner proved 11 records to be `logic:Nothing`, and purrdf's OWL-Direct consistency check agrees. There were two authoring errors.

## 1. `logic:message` values tagged against a plain-string range
- `logic:message` declares `rdfs:range xsd:string`, and 480 of its 497 values are plain strings. **17 carried `@x-gmeow-english`.** That makes them `rdf:langString`, which OWL 2 and RDF 1.1 make disjoint from `xsd:string`, so each record was unsatisfiable.
- Ten production records were proved `logic:Nothing` by two independent rules (`dl:datatype-membership-clash` and `refute:datatype-value-space`).
- **Fix:** untag the 17 outliers (10 in the logic slice, 7 slice-manifest constraints in `vocabulary.ttl`), keeping the precise range. That was chosen explicitly over widening or retyping the range.
- None of the 17 is an advice carrier bound verbatim to tagged source prose, and none was extracted into an i18n `.po` catalogue.

## 2. Thing-qualified counts on datatype properties
- 22 qualified cardinality restrictions on **datatype** properties named `logic:onClass logic:Thing`. OWL 2 keeps the object and data domains disjoint, so no literal can meet a Thing qualifier:
  - **`minQualifiedCardinality`** made every instance of its class **unsatisfiable**. The chase minted a resource witness for `lang:unicodeNormalization` and proved `gmeow:gatePolicyProse` `logic:Nothing` (`dl:datatype-property-literal-clash`).
  - **`maxQualifiedCardinality`** was **vacuous**: it counted Thing-valued successors a datatype property never has, so the intended at-most bound went unenforced.
- **Fix:** all 22 now qualify by `logic:onDataRange rdfs:Literal`, the form two existing restrictions already use. They span affect, agentic, calendar, gts, norms, images, lang and math.
- A corpus scan (872 datatype properties, both declaration layouts) finds none left.

## Checks
- Every changed file parses.
- The pre-commit hooks pass.
